text: The database layer proved healthy last lesson. This lesson finds what actually broke: the claims-processing app's own connection string.
Pulling the app's real configuration shows it hardcoded to the primary server's own hostname, not the failover group's listener built back in Lesson 11 to survive exactly this situation.
A SQL error 3906, database is read-only, confirms the diagnosis precisely: the app reached a real, healthy server -- just the wrong one for writes.
The fix repoints the connection string at the listener with ApplicationIntent=ReadWrite explicit. A second drill, watched end to end, proves the app now survives a failover with zero reconfiguration.
The connection string was the bug. The real root cause was a DR plan that had never been tested -- so a quarterly tested-failover drill gets scheduled going forward.
